items.slavonic_text: ходаще же про́повѣдаите гл̃юще · ꙗ́ко приближи сѧ цр̃тво небесное · болѧщиꙗ и́сцѣлꙗите · мрътвыꙗ въскрѣшаите · прокаженыꙗ ѡ́чѣщаите · тоу́не приꙗсте · тꙋне же и́ дадите :~ кн̃ · хвали :~ вънє вє̃ · стры · на г̃и въꙁва̃ · покаꙗнны · гла̃ є̃ подо́бны :~ Имѣꙗ бл̃гооу́тро́бїа и́сто́чннкы · и́ стачаꙗ же беꙁднꙋ мл̃остеи · и́ потокы щедрота · ѡ́че̃ прѣбл̃гыи , с̃не слово̃ , и́ д̃ше ст̃ыи · несꙋꙁданное е̃ство · приими маленїе и́ мл̃твоу нашꙋ · всѣмь и́же въ прегрѣшенїи соу́щи даꙗ прощенїе ꙗ́ко б̃ъ щедрыи и́ ч̃лколюбець :~ Имаши по естествоу ꙗ́ко б̃ъ · оу́тро́бꙋ щедро́ть · и́ миластель бл̃гостыни · тѣм же мл̃им тѧ х̃е сп̃се нашь · и́ припадаемь присно ꙁовемь въпию́ще · дароуи рабомь своим дль прѣгрѣшенїе · и́ прощенїе всѣмь · и́х же е̃съгрѣшихомь вси , ꙗ́ко б̃ъ щедрыи и́ ч̃лколюбець :~ Сп̃сти хо́тѧ всѣхъ · сп̃се ꙗ́ко б̃ъ · и́х же ради въ человѣчьскꙗ · ꙗ́вил се е̃си ꙗ́ко ч̃лкь · сп̃си насъ покланꙗющих сѧ твоимъ ꙁа́повѣдемь · не пришелъ бо е̃си ч̃лколюбче праведныхъ сп̃сти · нꙗ и́же въ прѣгрѣшенїихь ѡ́кованны · а́ насъ многими грѣхы · раꙁдрѣшити бл̃годатью крещенїа бж̃твънаго · ꙗ́ко б̃ъ щедрыи и́ ч̃лколюбець :~ і́ны бесплътныимь · тъжь · Свѣта свѣтлыми лоучями ѡ́свѣщаеми · бесплътныхъ чино́вь ·
items.english_text: *Gospel [Rubric: Gospel according to John; Witness: Matthew 10:1, 5–6]:* At that time, Jesus called His twelve disciples, and gave them power over unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal every infirmity and every disease among the people. These twelve Jesus sent forth, saying: Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and enter not into a city of the Samaritans; but go rather unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel; and as ye go, preach, saying: The Kingdom of heaven is at hand! Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers; freely ye have received, freely give![^148]

items.slavonic_text: славословатъ · въсѣчъскыимь влк̃оу всещедрителꙗ · ѿ несоу́щихъ въсѣ бл̃оудро́стью съдѣлавьшаго · а́рхагглнстїн · тѣхъ мл̃твами · ꙗ́ко единъ всеблаган бе · всемоу лироу мир посла · д̃шамь нашимь велию мл̃ть :~ Присно видꙗще бж̃їе лице · ѿ него просвѣщаеми · тресвѣтлыми ꙁарами · просвѣтите ны ѿ вѣкетра́стеин напастеин и́ꙁбавите · а́рхаггли стїн · тѣхъ мл̃твами бе · всемоу лироу мирь подан же · д̃шамь нашимь велі́ю мл̃ть :~ Божественую тр̃цꙋ · госпо́ствїе едино свѣдꙋщи · непрестанно славатъ · серафими же и́ херꙋви · вси а́гг̃ли а́рхггли · прѣстолни начала г̃ьства · беꙁьвещественныимоу́сты · коу́пно жен власти · мл̃ите х̃а · всемоу лироу мирь подан же · д̃шамь нашимь велию мл̃ть :~ сла̃ і́ нынкѣ :~ Страшна и́ прѣславна · велиа таина · невъмѣстимыи въ чрѣво твое въвлѣстисѧ · и́ м̃ти по рожествѣ д̃вою пакы пребысть · б̃а бо роди ниꙁне нас въпло́щьшаго сѧ · томоу въꙁъпиемь · томоу пѣснь рьцѣмь · съ а́гг̃лы въспѣвающе ст̃ъ еси х̃е б̃е въч̃лчивыисѧ насъ ради · г̃и слава тобѣ :~ на ст̃и покаꙗнны глась є · Г̃и съгрѣшаꙗ не престаю · ч̃лколюбїю сподоблаемь не раꙁоумѣю · ѡ́долѣн моемоу ѡ́мраченнїю · едине бл̃жен по́милоуи мѧ :~ Г̃и стра́ха твоего боюсѧ · и́ ꙁлое твора не престаю · кто на соуднщи
items.english_text: *Sticheron 4:* Enlightened by the radiant rays of Light, the ranks of the Bodiless hymn the Master of all, the All-Bountiful, Who made all things out of non-existence by wisdom, the Archangels with the Angels: by their prayers, as the only All-Good God, send peace unto all the world, and great mercy unto our souls![^149]

items.english_text: *Sticheron 5:* Ever beholding the face of God, enlightened by Him with thrice-radiant beams: enlighten us, and deliver us from the passions and temptations of the ages, O holy Archangels: by their prayers, O God, grant peace unto all the world, and great mercy unto our souls!

items.english_text: *Glory... Both now... Theotokion:* Fearful and most glorious is the great mystery: the Uncontainable was contained within thy womb, and as Mother after childbirth thou remainedst still a Virgin; for thou didst bear God Who came down and was incarnate for our sake! Unto Him let us cry aloud, unto Him let us sing a hymn, chanting with the Angels: Holy art Thou, O Christ God, Who wast made man for our sake; O Lord, glory to Thee!

items.slavonic_text: сꙋдии не оу́бо́ите сѧ · и́ли кто врачеванїꙗ хотѧ врача прогнѣваетъ · ꙗ́ко же а́ꙁъ дълготерпѣливе г̃и · на немощь д̃ша моꙗ оу́мл̃рди сѧ · и́ по́милоуи мѧ :~ Ѿ ꙁемныꙗ вѣкъ не брѣгше · и́ намꙋкы мꙋжескы волею дръꙁнꙋвше · бл̃женыи надежа не погрѣшисте · нъ нб̃сномоу цр̃твїю наслѣдници бысте · прѣхвалнїи м̃ч̃нци · и́мꙋще дръꙁновенїе къ мл̃тивомоу б̃оу · всемоу лироу ми́ра просите · д̃шамь наши велию мл̃ть :~ Ѡ́брадованнаа ходатанство · твоими мл̃твами · непросндшанїи · множество щедроть и́ ѡ́цѣщенїе · ѿ многыи съблаꙁнь нашии мл̃ита :~ В СЖБ ВЕЧЕРЬ НА ГИ ВЪЗВА постави , с̃ и́ · и́ по́е стры · въскр̃ны · гла̃ , ѕ̃ :~ Побѣдꙋ и́мын х̃е · е̃же на а́дъ на кр̃тъ въꙁыде да и́же сѣдѧщаꙗ въ тмѣ и́ сѣни съмрътнѣи · въскрѣсиши не съ собою · свободь и́нъ въ мрътвы · и́ стачаꙗ живо ѿ своего свѣта · всеси́лне сп̃се по́милоуи нас :~ Дн̃ь х̃с съ мр̃ть поправы · ꙗ́ко же рече и́ въскре · и́ радованнее всемоу лироу дарова · да вси къꙁывающи пѣснь длитѧ корцѣмь · и́сточниче жиꙁни · неприкосновенныи свѣте · въсеси́лне спасе по́милоуи насъ :~ Тебе г̃и соу́щаго по всеи твари · грѣшныи камо бѣжимъ · на небеси тоу самъ жи́веши · въ а́дѣ же поправы съ мр̃ть · въ глоубины мор
items.english_text: *Sticheron 2:* O Lord, I fear Thy dread judgment, yet doing evil I cease not; who at the judgment-seat fears not the judge? Or who that desires healing provokes the physician, as I do, O longsuffering Lord? Have compassion upon the weakness of my soul, and have mercy on me![^150]

items.english_text: *Martyrikon:* Disregarding the things of the earthly age, and manfully daring unto tortures of your own will: O blessed ones, ye missed not your hope, but became inheritors of the heavenly Kingdom, O all-praised Martyrs! Having boldness unto the merciful God, ask peace for all the world, and great mercy for our souls!

items.slavonic_text: сꙋдии не оу́бо́ите сѧ · и́ли кто врачеванїꙗ хотѧ врача прогнѣваетъ · ꙗ́ко же а́ꙁъ дълготерпѣливе г̃и · на немощь д̃ша моꙗ оу́мл̃рди сѧ · и́ по́милоуи мѧ :~ Ѿ ꙁемныꙗ вѣкъ не брѣгше · и́ намꙋкы мꙋжескы волею дръꙁнꙋвше · бл̃женыи надежа не погрѣшисте · нъ нб̃сномоу цр̃твїю наслѣдници бысте · прѣхвалнїи м̃ч̃нци · и́мꙋще дръꙁновенїе къ мл̃тивомоу б̃оу · всемоу лироу ми́ра просите · д̃шамь наши велию мл̃ть :~ Ѡ́брадованнаа ходатанство · твоими мл̃твами · непросндшанїи · множество щедроть и́ ѡ́цѣщенїе · ѿ многыи съблаꙁнь нашии мл̃ита :~ В СЖБ ВЕЧЕРЬ НА ГИ ВЪЗВА постави , с̃ и́ · и́ по́е стры · въскр̃ны · гла̃ , ѕ̃ :~ Побѣдꙋ и́мын х̃е · е̃же на а́дъ на кр̃тъ въꙁыде да и́же сѣдѧщаꙗ въ тмѣ и́ сѣни съмрътнѣи · въскрѣсиши не съ собою · свободь и́нъ въ мрътвы · и́ стачаꙗ живо ѿ своего свѣта · всеси́лне сп̃се по́милоуи нас :~ Дн̃ь х̃с съ мр̃ть поправы · ꙗ́ко же рече и́ въскре · и́ радованнее всемоу лироу дарова · да вси къꙁывающи пѣснь длитѧ корцѣмь · и́сточниче жиꙁни · неприкосновенныи свѣте · въсеси́лне спасе по́милоуи насъ :~ Тебе г̃и соу́щаго по всеи твари · грѣшныи камо бѣжимъ · на небеси тоу самъ жи́веши · въ а́дѣ же поправы съ мр̃ть · въ глоубины мор
items.english_text: *Theotokion:* O rejoice-filled Mediatress: by thy prayers, without ceasing, ask a multitude of bounties and cleansing from our many stumbling-blocks!

items.office: On Saturday Evening, at "Lord, I have cried," set 8 stichoi, and sing the Resurrection Stichera, Tone 6

items.english_text: *Sticheron 1:* Having the victory over Hades, O Christ, Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, that Thou mightest raise with Thyself those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death: free among the dead, and pouring forth life from Thine own light: O Almighty Savior, have mercy on us!

items.english_text: *Sticheron 2:* Today Christ, having trampled down death, is risen even as He said, and has granted rejoicing unto all the world, that all, crying aloud, may send up a hymn: O Fountain of life, Unapproachable Light, Almighty Savior, have mercy on us!

items.office: On Saturday Evening, at "Lord, I have cried," set 8 stichoi, and sing the Resurrection Stichera, Tone 6
items.slavonic_text: рескыꙗ · и́ тоу рꙋка твоꙗ влк̃о · к тебѣ прибѣгаемь · и́ тобѣ припадающе мо́лим сѧ въскръсыин и́ꙁъмртвы · сп̃се по́милоуи насъ :~ натолнци :~ Кр̃тꙋ твои х̃е хвалим сѧ · и́ въскресенїе твое поемь и́ слави · ты бо еси к̃ъ нашь · раꙁвѣ бо тебе и́но́го не ꙁнае̃ :~ Слава силѣ твоеи г̃и · ꙗ́ко раꙁдроу́ши дръжавоу и́моу́щаго съ мр̃ти · ѡ́бновиль еси насъ кр̃тѡ свои и́ дарова на̃ животъ и́ нетленне :~ Въ и́стинноу бл̃агосло́ваще г̃а · пое̃ въскресенне е̃го · распѧтне бо притръпѣ · и́ съ мрътнию съ мрътъ раꙁдроу́ши :~ Погре́бенне твое х̃е · оу́ꙁы а́довы съкроу́шивъ ра́ꙁврѣже · и́ е̃же и́ꙁ мрътвы въскренне · въ сего лира просвѣти · ч̃лколюбче слава тобѣ :~ по вто̃ · е̃ ди̃ :~ Кто тебе не бл̃жить прѣс̃таа д̃во · и́ли кто не въспѣва́етъ тво́е чистаго рожества беꙁ лѣтныи бо ѡ́ ѿц̃а въ сїꙗвы с̃нъ единоро́дныи · тожде ѿ тебе чистыꙗ проиде · неиꙁречено въпло́щьшесѧ естествомъ б̃ъ сыи · е̃стество̃ бывы ч̃лкъ на ради · не въ двѣ лицн раꙁдѣлаемы · и́ ж въ дв̃ю нꙋне е̃стество неоу́копоꙁнаваема · то́го моли чистаа и́ б̃гобл̃женаꙗ по́миловатисѧ д̃шамь нашимь :~ на ст̃ивнѣ стры · гла̃ , ѕ̃ Въскренїе твое х̃е сп̃се · а́гг̃ли поютъ на нб̃сѣ · и́ на на ꙁемли и́сподоби · чистыимь ср̃це̃мь тебе пѣти и́ славити :~ по і́ꙁвидѣ :~ Врата а́дова на ма съкроушини еси г̃и · и́ верѣꙗ а́довы
items.english_text: *Sticheron 3:* Whither shall we sinners flee from Thee, O Lord, Who art throughout all creation? In heaven, there Thou Thyself dwellest; in Hades, Thou didst trample down death; into the depths of the sea there also is Thy hand, O Master! Unto Thee do we flee, and falling down before Thee, we pray, O Thou Who didst rise from the dead: O Savior, have mercy on us![^151]

items.office: On Saturday Evening, at "Lord, I have cried," set 8 stichoi, and sing the Resurrection Stichera, Tone 6

items.english_text: *Sticheron 3:* Desiring to correct the corruption of ancient ruin, Christ was nailed upon the Cross and laid in the tomb. Him the myrrh-bearing women sought with tears, and weeping they said: "Woe to us, O Savior, King of all! How didst Thou deign to dwell in a tomb? And having dwelt there of Thine Own will, how wast Thou stolen away? What manner of place hid Thy life-bearing body? Yea, appear, even as Thou didst promise us, appear unto us, and stay our tearful weeping!" But while they wept, an Angel cried aloud unto them: "Cease from weeping! Go, tell the Apostles that Christ is risen, granting resurrection and great mercy unto the world!"

items.english_text: Brethren: Such a High Priest was fitting for us, Who is holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; Who has no need daily, as the high priests, to offer up sacrifices, first for His own sins, and then for those of the people: for this He did once for all when He offered up Himself. For the law appoints men high priests having infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was after the law, appoints the Son, perfected unto ages of ages. Now of the things spoken this is the sum: We have such a High Priest, Who is seated on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens; a Minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.

items.english_text: The Lord said: "I am the door: by Me if anyone enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. The thief comes not, but to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life. I am the Good Shepherd: the Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep. But he that is a hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, sees the wolf coming, and leaves the sheep, and flees; and the wolf catches them,[^173] and scatters the sheep. The hireling flees, because he is a hireling, and cares not for the sheep. I am the Good Shepherd, and know Mine, even as the Father knows Me, and I know the Father; and I lay down My life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear My voice; and there shall be one flock, and one Shepherd."

items.english_text: *Troparion:* Having received eternal redemption through thee, O Virgin, with diligence we cry aloud unto thee: "Rejoice, O Sovereign Lady!" and rejoicing in thy light, we hymn thee with songs!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Ode 6. Heirmos:*[^195] Voyaging in the tempest of life without wind, and being submerged like a ship by sins, and cast about by the soul-corrupting whirlpool, crying like Jonah, O Christ: "Lead me up from the death-bearing deep!"

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Troparion:* The earthly congregation having of old been sold by polytheistic deceit, Thou, the Son of God, didst come in the form of a servant, and wast lifted up upon the Cross, O Christ, that Thou mightest deliver [us] from corruption, as Thou art merciful!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.slavonic_text: въспѣваемь : ~ Е́диноутꙗ жени хъ · посреди тръ
items.english_text: *Theotokion:* Who among men can declare the image of thine ineffable birthgiving, O spotless one, O Virgin Bride of God, for our sake? For the ineffable Word united Himself [to flesh] from thee, and the flesh remained unchangeable!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)
items.slavonic_text: ꙗ́ко бл̃гъ · лютаꙗ мꙗ съгрѣшенїа : ~ С̃мо̃рть раꙁо
items.english_text: *Another Canon of the Cross. Heirmos: I cried unto Thee...* When Thou wast crucified, O Master, the whole earth was shaken, and as Thou art good, Thou didst heal my grievous transgressions!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Theotokion:* O most pure Sovereign Lady, strong hope of Christians: preserve those who sing of thee with love, as one loving the truth!

items.english_text: *Another Canon to the Most Holy Theotokos. Same Heirmos:* The prophetic prophecies manifestly proclaimed by legal types that thou wouldst give birth unto the Blessing of all creation, Who in many and manifold ways did good unto those who faithfully sing of thee!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Troparion:* Adam the first-formed, who of old was frightened away by the counsel of the murderer of man from the divine food of paradise, thou didst manifestly lead back, O unwedded one, having given birth unto Him Who delivered us from his transgression!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Troparion:* The Divine Light, Who by His all-effective power brought all things into being out of nothing, came forth from thy womb, O pure one, and shone with divine radiance upon those sitting in the darkness of death!

items.english_text: *Ode 7. Heirmos:* Of old the Children showed the fiery-burning furnace to be breathing dew, singing to the one God and saying: "O God of our fathers, Who art supremely exalted, blessed art Thou!"

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Troparion:* By the tree he who committed disobedience is put to death, but by the obedience of Christ he is formed anew; for for my sake the all-glorious Son of God is crucified!

items.english_text: *Theotokion:* Rejoice, daughter of corruptible Adam! Rejoice, only Bride of God! Rejoice, through whom the curse was banished, for thou didst bear God; entreat Him, O pure one, to save us all!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Another Canon of the Cross. Heirmos: In the Chaldean furnace...* Of Thine own will Thou wast crucified upon the Cross, that Thou mightest free men from corruption; therefore, pouring forth hymns, [we cry]: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers!"

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

Heirmos:* The bush unconsumed by fire in Sinai, communing [therewith], showed forth God unto slow-tongued and stammering Moses; and the Children cast into the fire with divine zeal showed forth singers: "All ye works of the Lord, hymn the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Troparion:* With the saving Blood, His own precious Blood, wherewith He redeemed us who had fallen through deceit, and destroyed the deceitful torment of the fierce enemy: therefore we unceasingly magnify Thee!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: *Troparion:* Thou didst endure death by the spear,[^200] O Compassionate One, and didst come forth from the tomb as a bridegroom from the bridal chamber, and didst grant us incorruption: therefore we unceasingly magnify Thee!

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)
items.slavonic_text: всꙗ дѣла г̃ни г̃а поите : ~ Свѣта твоего лоучами

items.office: SUNDAY MIDNIGHT OFFICE (TONE 7)

items.english_text: Brethren: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, patience, goodness, gentleness, unfeignedness; against such there is no law. And they that are Christ Jesus' have crucified the flesh with the passions and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit; and let us not be desirous of vainglory, despising one another, envying one another. And if a man be overtaken in any fault, ye who are spiritual, restore such a one in the spirit of gentleness, considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted. Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

items.english_text: *Epistle to the Corinthians [1 Cor. 1:10–18]:*[^247] Brethren, I beseech you by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you; but that ye be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment. For it has been declared unto me of you, my brethren, by them of the household of Chloe, that there are contentions among you. Now this I say, that every one of you says: "I am of Paul," and "I of Apollos," and "I of Cephas," and "I of Christ." Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were ye baptized in the name of Paul? I thank my God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius, lest anyone should say that I baptized in mine own name. And I baptized also the household of Stephanas; besides, I know not whether I baptized any other. For Christ sent me not to baptize, but to preach the Gospel: not in wisdom of words, lest the Cross of Christ should be made of none effect. For the word of the Cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us who are saved it is the power of God.

items.english_text: *Gospel according to John [John 15:17–16:2]:*[^249] The Lord said unto His disciples: These things I command you, that ye love one another. If the world hate you, know that it hated Me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love its own; but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. Remember the word that I said unto you: The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted Me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept My word, they will keep yours also. But all these things will they do unto you for My name's sake, because they know not Him Who sent Me. If I had not come and spoken unto them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin. He that hates Me hates My Father also. If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they would not have had sin; but now have they both seen and hated both Me and My Father. But this comes to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law: "They hated Me without a cause." But when the Comforter is come, Whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, Who proceeds from the Father, He shall testify of Me; and ye also shall bear witness, because ye have been with Me from the beginning. These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be offended. They shall put you out of the synagogues; yea, the time comes, that whosoever kills you will think that he offers service unto God.

items.english_text: *Epistle to the Hebrews [Heb. 2:2–10]:* Brethren, if the word spoken by angels was steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense of reward, how shall we escape, if we neglect so great a salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard Him; God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with various miracles, and distributions of the Holy Spirit, according to His own will? For He did not put in subjection unto the angels the world to come, whereof we speak. But one in a certain place testified, saying: "What is man, that Thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that Thou visitest him? Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; Thou crownedst him with glory and honor, and didst set him over the works of Thy hands; Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet." For in that He put all in subjection under him, He left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him. But we see Jesus, Who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honor; that He by the grace of God should taste death for every man. For it became Him, for Whom are all things, and by Whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the Captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

items.english_text: *Gospel according to John [sic! Matthew 13:24–30, 36–43]:*[^265] The Lord spoke unto His disciples this parable: The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man who sowed good seed in his field; but while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way. But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also. So the servants of the householder came and said unto him: "Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then does it have tares?" He said unto them: "An enemy has done this." The servants said unto him: "Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up?" But he said: "Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest; and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers: Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them; but gather the wheat into my barn." And His disciples came unto Him, saying: "Declare unto us the parable of the tares of the field." He answered and said unto them: "He Who sows the good seed is the Son of man; the field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; the enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels. As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world. The Son of man shall send forth His angels, and they shall gather out of His kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity; and shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth. Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He that has ears to hear, let him hear."

items.english_text: *Epistle from the Acts of the Apostles [Acts 13:25–33]:* In those days, when John was finishing his course, he said: Whom think ye that I am? I am not He; but behold, there comes One after me, the strap of Whose sandals I am not worthy to unloose. Men, brethren, sons of the family of Abraham, and whosoever among you fears God, unto you is the word of this salvation sent. For they who dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, having not understood Him, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every Sabbath day, have fulfilled them by condemning Him. And having found no cause of death in Him, they desired of Pilate that He should be slain. And when they had fulfilled all that was written of Him, they crucified Him; and taking Him down from the Tree, they laid Him in a tomb. But God raised Him from the dead; Who was seen for many days by those who came up with Him from Galilee unto Jerusalem, who are His witnesses unto the people. And we declare unto you the good tidings of the promise which was made unto the fathers, that God hath fulfilled the same unto their children, having raised up Jesus for us.

items.english_text: Brethren, Abraham had two sons, the one by a bondmaid, the other by a freewoman. But he who was of the bondwoman was born after the flesh; but he of the freewoman was by promise. Which things are an allegory: for these are the two covenants; the one from Mount Sinai, which genders to bondage, which is Hagar. For this Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and answers to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children. But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all. For it is written, Rejoice, thou barren that bearest not; break forth and cry, thou that travailest not: for the desolate hath many more children than she which hath an husband.[^295] Now we, brethren, as Isaac was, are the children of promise. But as then he that was born after the flesh persecuted him that was born after the Spirit, even so it is now. Nevertheless what says the scripture? Cast out the bondwoman and her son: for the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with the son of the freewoman. So then, brethren, we are not children of the bondwoman, but of the free. Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free.

items.english_text: At that time, Jesus entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received Him into her house. And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus' feet, and heard His word. But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to Him, and said, Lord, dost Thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me. And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: but one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her. And it came to pass, as He spake these things, a certain woman of the company lifted up her voice, and said unto Him, Blessed is the womb that bare Thee, and the paps which Thou hast sucked. But He said, Yea rather, blessed are they that hear the word of God, and keep it.

items.english_text: Brethren: God hath displayed us, the apostles, last, as it were appointed unto death; for we have been made a spectacle unto the world, both to angels and to men. We are fools for Christ’s sake, but ye are wise in Christ; we are weak,[^310] but ye are strong; ye are honorable, but we are despised. Even unto this present hour we both hunger, and thirst, and are naked, and are buffeted, and have no certain dwelling-place; and labor, working with our own hands: being reviled, we bless; being persecuted, we endure it; being defamed, we entreat: we are made as the filth of the world, and are the offscouring of all things unto this day. I write not these things to shame you, but as my beloved children I warn you. For though ye have ten thousand instructors in Christ, yet have ye not many fathers: for in Christ Jesus I have begotten you through the Gospel. Therefore I beseech you, be ye followers of me.

items.english_text: Brethren: The preaching of the Cross is to them that perish foolishness; but unto us which are saved it is the power of God. For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent. Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this world? Hath not God made foolish the wisdom of this world? For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks seek after wisdom: but we preach Christ crucified, unto the Jews a stumblingblock, and unto the Greeks foolishness; but unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.[^326]

items.english_text: *Tone 8 (Doxasticon of the Departed by St. John of Damascus):* I weep and I wail when I contemplate death, and behold our beauty, fashioned according to the image of God, lying in the tombs, disfigured, inglorious, having neither form nor comeliness. Truly by the command of God, as it is written, Who grants rest unto the departed.[^329]

items.english_text: *Epistle of the Holy Apostle Paul to the Thessalonians (Departed) [1 Thess. 4:13–17]:* Brethren, I would not have you to be ignorant concerning those who are fallen asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others who have no hope; for if[^340] we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so those also who sleep in Jesus will God bring with Him. For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we who are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent those who are asleep. For the Lord Himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet of God; and the dead in Christ shall rise first. Then we who are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air; and so shall we ever be with the Lord.

items.english_text: *Gospel according to Matthew (Departed) [John 5:24–30]:* The Lord said unto the Jews who came unto Him: Truly, truly, I say unto you: He that hears My word, and believes on Him that sent Me, has everlasting life, and shall not come into judgment, but is passed from death unto life. Truly, truly, I say unto you: The hour comes, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God; and they that hear shall live. For as the Father has life in Himself, so has He given to the Son to have life in Himself; and has given Him authority to execute judgment also, because He is the Son of Man. Marvel not at this; for the hour comes, in which all that are in the graves shall hear the voice of the Son of God, and shall come forth: they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life[^341] and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment. I can of Mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge; and My judgment is just, because I seek not Mine own will, but the will of the Father Who sent Me.

items.english_text: *Second Matins Resurrection Gospel, from Mark [Mark 16:1–8]:* At that time, when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint Jesus. And very early in the morning the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun. And they said among themselves: Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre? And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away: for it was very great. And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment; and they were affrighted. And he says unto them: Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, Who was crucified: He is risen; He is not here: behold the place where they laid Him. But go your way, tell His disciples and Peter that He goes before you into Galilee: there shall ye see Him, as He said unto you. And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre; for they trembled and were amazed: neither said they any thing to any man; for they were afraid.

items.english_text: *Third Matins Resurrection Gospel, from Mark [Mark 16:9–20]:* At that time, when Jesus was risen early the first day of the week, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom He had cast seven devils. And she went and told them that had been with Him, as they mourned and wept. And they, when they had heard that He was alive, and had been seen of her, believed not. After that He appeared in another form unto two of them, as they walked, and went into the country. And they went[^344] and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them. Afterward He appeared unto the eleven as they sat at meat, and upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they believed not them which had seen Him after He was risen. And He said unto them: Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature. He that believes and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believes not shall be condemned. And these signs shall follow them that believe: In My name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues; they shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover. So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, He was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God. And they went forth, and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following. Amen.

items.english_text: *Fourth Matins Resurrection Gospel, from Luke [Luke 24:1–12]:* Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them. And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre. And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus. And it came to pass, as they were much perplexed thereabout, behold, two men stood by them in shining garments: and as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them: Why seek ye the living among the dead? He is not here, but is risen: remember how He spake unto you when He was yet in Galilee, saying: The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again. And they remembered His words, and returned from the sepulchre, and told all these things unto the eleven[^346] and to all the rest. It was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and other women that were with them, which told these things unto the apostles. And their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not. Then arose Peter, and ran unto the sepulchre; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass.

items.english_text: *Fifth Matins Resurrection Gospel, from Luke [Luke 24:12–35]:* At that time, then arose Peter, and ran unto the sepulchre; and stooping down, he beheld the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed, wondering in himself at that which was come to pass. And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs. And they talked together of all these things which had happened. And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus Himself drew near, and went with them. But their eyes were holden that they should not know Him. And He said unto them: What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto Him: Art Thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? And He said unto them: What things? And they said unto Him: Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, Which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered Him to be condemned to death, and have crucified Him. But we trusted that it had been He which should have redeemed Israel: and beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done. Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; and when they found not His body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels[^348] which said that He was alive. And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but Him they saw not. And He said unto them: O foolish men, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into His glory? And beginning at Moses and all the prophets, He expounded unto them in all the scriptures the things concerning Himself. And they drew nigh unto the village, whither they went: and He made as though He would go further. But they constrained Him, saying: Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is already far spent. And He went in to tarry with them. And it came to pass, as He sat at meat with them, He took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. And their eyes were opened, and they knew Him; and He became invisible unto them. And they said one to another: Did not our heart burn within us, while He talked with us by the way, and while He expounded unto us the scriptures? And they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them, saying: The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon! And they told what things were done in the way, and how He was known of them in breaking of bread.

items.english_text: *Sixth Matins Resurrection Gospel, from Luke [Luke 24:36–53]:* At that time, Jesus, being risen from the dead, stood in the midst of them, and said unto them: Peace be unto you. But they were terrified and affrighted, and supposed that they had seen a spirit. And He said unto them: Why are ye troubled? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? Behold My hands and My feet, that it is I Myself: handle Me, and see; for a spirit has not flesh and bones, as ye see Me have. And when He had thus spoken[^350] He showed them His hands and His feet. And while they yet believed not for joy, and wondered, He said unto them: Have ye here any meat? And they gave Him a piece of a broiled fish, and of an honeycomb. And He took it, and did eat before them. And He said unto them: These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning Me. Then opened He their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures, and said unto them: Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: and that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in His name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. And ye are witnesses of these things. And, behold, I send the promise of My Father upon you: but tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high. And He led them out as far as to Bethany, and He lifted up His hands, and blessed them. And it came to pass, while He blessed them, He was parted from them, and carried up into heaven. And they worshipped Him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy: and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

items.english_text: *Seventh Matins Resurrection Gospel, from John [John 20:1–10]:* At that time, the first day of the week came Mary Magdalene early, when it was yet dark, unto the sepulchre, and saw the stone taken away from the sepulchre. Then she ran, and came to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and said unto them: They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid Him. Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulchre. So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre. And he stooping down, saw the linen clothes lying[^352] yet went he not in. Then came Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and saw the linen clothes lie, and the napkin, that was about His head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself. Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed. For as yet they knew not the scripture, that He must rise again from the dead. Then the disciples went away again unto their own home.

items.english_text: *Eighth Matins Resurrection Gospel, from John [John 20:11–18]:* At that time, Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping: and as she wept, she stooped down, and looked into the sepulchre, and saw two angels in white sitting, the one at the head, and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain. And they said unto her: Woman, why weepest thou? and whom seekest thou? She said unto them: Because they have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid Him. And when she had thus said, she turned herself back, and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus. Jesus said unto her: Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing Him to be the gardener, said unto Him: Sir, if Thou have borne Him hence, tell me where Thou hast laid Him, and I will take Him away. Jesus said unto her: Mary. She turned herself, and said unto Him: Rabboni; which is to say, Master. Jesus said unto her: Touch Me not; for I am not yet ascended to My Father: but go to My brethren, and say unto them: I ascend unto My Father, and your Father; and to My God, and your God. Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that He had spoken these things unto her.

items.english_text: *Ninth Matins Resurrection Gospel, from John [John 20:19–31]:* Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and said unto them: Peace be unto you. And when He had so said, He showed unto them His hands and His feet and His side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord. Then said Jesus to them again: Peace be unto you: as My Father hath sent Me, even so send I you. And when He had said this, He breathed on them, and said unto them: Receive ye the Holy Spirit: whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained. But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came. The other disciples therefore said unto him: We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them: Except I shall see in His hands the print of the nails[^355] and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into His side, I will not believe. And after eight days again His disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said: Peace be unto you. Then said He to Thomas: Reach hither thy finger, and behold My hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into My side: and be not faithless, but believing. And Thomas answered and said unto Him: My Lord and my God. Jesus said unto him: Thomas, because thou hast seen Me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed. And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book: but these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through His name.

items.english_text: *Tenth Matins Resurrection Gospel, from John [John 21:1–14]:* At that time, Jesus showed Himself again to the disciples, being risen from the dead, at the Sea of Tiberias; and on this wise showed He Himself: there were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of His disciples. Simon Peter said unto them: I go a fishing. They say unto him: We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. Then Jesus said unto them: Children, have ye any meat? They answered Him: No. And He said unto them: Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes. Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved said unto Peter: It is the Lord! Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his fisher's coat unto him (for he was naked), and did cast himself into the sea. And the other disciples[^357] came in a little ship (for they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits), dragging the net with fishes. As soon then as they were come to land, they saw a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread. Jesus said unto them: Bring of the fish which ye have now caught. Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land full of great fishes, an hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, yet was not the net broken. Jesus said unto them: Come and dine. And none of the disciples durst ask Him: Who art Thou? knowing that it was the Lord. Jesus then came, and took bread, and gave them, and fish likewise. This is now the third time that Jesus showed Himself to His disciples, after that He was risen from the dead.

items.english_text: *Eleventh Matins Resurrection Gospel, from John [John 21:15–25]:* At that time, Jesus showed Himself to His disciples, after that He was risen from the dead; and said to Simon Peter: Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me more than these? He said unto Him: Yea, Lord; Thou knowest that I love Thee. He said unto him: Feed My lambs. He said to him again the second time: Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me? He said unto Him: Yea, Lord; Thou knowest that I love Thee. He said unto him: Feed My sheep. He said unto him the third time: Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me? Peter was grieved because He said unto him the third time, Lovest thou Me? And he said unto Him: Lord, Thou knowest all things; Thou knowest that I love Thee. Jesus said unto him: Feed My sheep. Truly, truly, I say unto thee: When thou wast young, thou didst gird thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest; but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not. This spake He, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when He had spoken this, He said unto him: Follow Me. Then Peter, turning[^359] about, sees the disciple whom Jesus loved following; which also leaned on His breast at supper, and said: Lord, which is he that betrays Thee? Peter seeing him said to Jesus: Lord, and what shall this man do? Jesus said unto him: If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou Me. Then went this saying abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but: If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? This is the disciple which testifies of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true. And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which, if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself could not contain the books that should be written. Amen.

items.english_text: Consider, brethren, and shudder in fear, O men! For we are about to give an accounting at the last, on the dreadful Day of Judgment. We shall stand compunctious and downcast, condemned by our evil deeds which we committed in this life, which it befits not Christians to commit—these evil deeds from which we renounced ourselves at baptism, saying: "We renounce Satan and all his works." Therefore let us abide in God and before the angels of God, having cast away from ourselves all evil and unfitting things, and acting in fear, in meekness, and in divine love. Yea, brethren, let us all weep for ourselves, and mourn, and sigh deeply, that we may be preserved from the burning river of fire!

items.english_text: *Woe is me!* Woe is me, a sinner and wretched! What awaitest thou, O accursed soul, full of all filth? How wilt thou answer the Judge? Where wilt thou hide thine iniquitous deeds?

items.english_text: *Woe is me, a sinner and wretched!* How am I humble in opinion, but always there is boldness, and there is no submission, but always pride; and there is no fasting, neither prostrations; unmerciful, unclean, having neither faith nor uprightness, neither mercy nor love! How then, O soul, dost thou desire to obtain mercy, seeing that thou art full of all evil?

items.office: On Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Prophets and Martyrs, Tone 8.

items.english_text: Woe is me! what I shall do, I know not. Seeing men fasting unto God and bowing down, and doing works of mercy, and walking in meekness and knowingly in the fear of God—I did not perceive, and through my weakness saw not; and seeing their self-restraint, I did not emulate them, but turned away from them unto evil and destruction, and reviled all the servants of God with a deceitful tongue and an evil heart! How then do I desire to be saved? Seeing men who are weak, I lent an ear to them, and loved them with my heart[^368] and I joined myself unto them unto evil and unto the perdition of my soul!

items.office: On Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Prophets and Martyrs, Tone 8.
items.slavonic_text: Ѡхъ мнѣ небогоу • да тѣлоу оугодное сътворихъ •
items.english_text: Oh, woe is me, wretched one! for I did what was pleasing to the flesh by mine evil deeds, by unfaithfulness and greediness, and I myself drown my soul in eternal torment! Oh, woe is me, O soul: amend thyself at least from henceforth! Oh, woe is me, wretched one: how was I deprived of honor, and of what kind of glory, what brightness was I willing to lose through mine own lack of fear! Why, O soul, dost thou not give ear to the instruction of the Lord and of the holy venerable fathers, but ever turnest aside unto evil? Oh, O soul, hast thou heard the bitter answer, saying: "It is not good with others"? Fear that answer!

items.office: On Friday evening, at "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Prophets and Martyrs, Tone 8.
items.slavonic_text: ꙗко пострадасте тако приидѣте • слышастели
items.english_text: Do thou therefore tremble, O accursed and defiled soul, that art defiled at all hours! Why weepest thou not, O man? Think upon the life of this deceitful world: today thou livest and makest merry, and tomorrow thou shalt die, and rot, and be dust! From earth, into earth shalt thou go. O wretched man, [destroying] through thine own weakness even thy priceless soul, O wretched man! Hast thou not heard the Lord God calling the righteous, and the meek, and the merciful: "Blessed are the poor in spirit; they that weep for My sake; blessed are they that hunger; blessed are the merciful; blessed are the pure; blessed are ye when they shall say all manner of evil word against you; endure for My sake; rejoice and be glad; come, ye blessed[^369] even as ye suffered, so come ye!" Have ye heard, dear brethren? What again shall the glorious and sluggish receive regarding Christ's commandments? Those indeed shall enter into eternal torments; then shall the righteous, the meek, and the obedient to Christ's commandments receive, entering into eternal life. Therefore, knowing this, brethren, let us not give ourselves over to worldly joys through our lusts, but unto ascetic struggles for the sake of our salvation, glorifying unceasingly the Trinity: Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.

items.english_text: Chastise thy son in his youth, and he shall give thee rest in thine old age, and shall give beauty unto thy soul. Relax not over a child; for even if thou strike him with a rod, he shall not die, but shall be healthier; for striking him in body, thou shalt deliver his soul from death. Hast thou daughters? place thy strictness upon them; if thou preserve them not in bodily purity, thou mayest bring shame upon thy face. For if thou give a daughter in marriage without blemish, thou shalt have accomplished a great work, and in the midst of the assembly[^370] thou shalt be praised, and at her end thou shalt not groan over her. For he that loves his son causes him frequent blows, that he may afterwards rejoice over him. Chastise thy son from his youth, and thou shalt rejoice in him in his manhood, and in the midst of the assembly thou shalt boast of him, and envy shall seize thine enemies. And rear a child with discipline, and thou shalt find rest and blessing in him. Laugh not, playing with him, for in a little matter thou wilt smile, but in a great matter thou wilt grieve, gnashing thy teeth, and at the last it shall set thy soul's teeth on edge. Give him not authority in his youth, and crush not his ribs while he is growing up, lest becoming hardened he disobey thee, and thou have vexation from him, and grief of soul, and loss to thy household, and ruin of possessions, and reproach from neighbors, and mockery before enemies and before magistrates, fines and sore grief.

items.english_text: Consider, brethren, what fear we ought to have in that world, on the Day of Judgment! For we shall stand compunctious because of our evil deeds which we did in this life: weeping, playing, acting foolishly, and making merry, which it behoves not Christians to do. First of all, be not deceived, saying: "If God had commanded neither to drink nor to eat[^371] nor to make merry, then why did He create the world upon the earth?" Give ear unto me, what I say unto you: The Prophet Elijah saw neither bread, nor wine, nor human joy; he left all and went unto the mountain, and went unto the mountain, and fasted forty days; and was he not taken up into heaven by these deeds? And the other Prophet, Daniel, had no portion in his own house; having the king's dreams in his hands, much gold, and all manner of goods, walrus tusks, and precious stones—and leaving all these things, he filled the depth of his heart, and opened the earthly life; and when the rulers grew angry with him and cast him unto the lions, the lions ran with haste and licked his feet; and when he was in distress, the Holy Spirit came and snatched him thence!

items.english_text: O ye senseless men, in what do ye trust, and repent not, and walk with pride and with smallness of soul, being burdened with gorging, casting down your soul with haughtiness? Why hast thou no mercy on thyself? Why dost thou not sigh unto the Heavenly King, Who is the Dominion of all creation, and the Creator of heaven and earth?

items.english_text: Understand, O brethren: he that thirsts here, drinks there; he that eats not here, shall be filled there; he that is compunctious here, shall be joyful there; he that is of a contrite heart here, shall there be established in glorious praise.

items.english_text: O my brethren, restrain your tongue from much speaking; restrain your eyes from much gazing; strengthen your ears from much listening. Oh, woe is me, brethren! [I lament] over the tormented soul which weeps as in a deep well within its body, which is fattened by mine evil deeds!

items.english_text: O my brethren, let us cry aloud with tears and with heavy sighing unto Jesus Christ the Savior of God: He is able to heal the possessed, and the blind, and the sick, and He raised him that was dead four days! For He is able to renew heaven and earth, and to set men in their proper orders.

items.english_text: O my brethren, see and understand what things the Master endured from mankind: mockery and crucifixion! Like senseless men, know ye not that in sins were we conceived, and in sins were we born? Give ear unto me, and answer, saying: "We have spent our years and days, and have had our fill"; and be not able to say: "We cannot bend the knee", for answers are prepared for you[^373] O senseless men: "Where wast thou when I made the angelic ranks and all the earth? Where wast thou when He planted His vineyard?"

items.english_text: O brethren, be not deceived, saying: "Now we are despondent, let us rejoice and make merry, and tomorrow we shall repent!" Know ye not, brethren, that as the dew is dried up from the face [of the earth], so also your youth is dried up by evil deeds?

items.english_text: Lo, I say unto you now: When thou sleepest, if a thief should come upon thy house, if one stood by, he would not suffer him to approach it. Even so I say unto you, brethren: Watch with fear, lest when the angel comes, he snatch away your soul, and your haste be in vain, so that it cannot look back to repent!

items.english_text: Therefore now I say unto you: Receive this instruction, write it in the depth of your hearts, meditate upon it all days and nights, and call upon the Lord at all hours, saying: "O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, draw near Thy mercy, and fence my soul as with a strong wall of iron, that mine enemy snatch me not away like a roaring lion!"
